doc.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Pop sessions and the hit-record question
title: Billy Joel, Phoebe Snow and Aretha sessions
summary: Phil Ramone books him; 'Just the Way You Are' earns only $300.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: What was the first one I did? I was a good friend of Phil Ramone’s and he got me the gig with uh with Billy Joel. “Just the Way You Are.” And Phoebe Snow, I did Phoebe Snow and Billy Joel in the same session. It was just me and Phil in the studio and he had the changes on the back of a matchbook cover, you know. And the Billy Joel thing is like a pop song, and Phoebe Snow was okay. And he got me an Aretha Franklin … [sings da da da da]
“Somewhere,” which really came out nice, I think.

I love that record. But the Billy Joel really all of a sudden it’s the biggest selling record in history, you know. And wow, you know? I mean, I heard my solo all over the world. In fact, my solo is in the piano music, you know. And I made a grand total of 300 dollars. [both laugh] You know, Billy got a lot more than that. In fact, I ran across a lawyer from California that said, “Did Billy Joel take care of you?” I said, “What do you mean?” I said, “No, I didn’t get a cufflink, a chocolate, nothin’.” He said, “That’s strange, because Billy was going to send you a check.” And then it came out a little later on, right after this guy said that, that Billy Joel’s manager ripped him off, stole all his bread. I mean, he really took a hit from the manager and I got, ‘cause Billy Joel’s a pretty good guy, and I got a feeling that Billy said, “Send Phil a check” you know, ‘cause he’s an important part of the record. And the manager said, “Oh, sure,” and, you know, stuck it in his own pocket. So, but I mean I heard, I was in the middle of Warsaw and I heard that in a Polish hotel, a guy playing my solo. Every time I hear it I’d go up and say nice job on my solo and they’d say, “Oh my god, it’s him!” You know. But the best one though is, I was working
